title: Protocol for live imaging of intracellular nanoscale structures using atomic force microscopy with nanoneedle probes
protocol: Seed 0.1–5 × 10^4 BALB/3T3 cells on a 35 mm low-height glass-bottomed dish in culture medium.
Culture cells in a 5% CO2 incubator for 2 days.
Prepare 1 mM SiR-Actin stock solution by dissolving the reagent in anhydrous Dimethyl sulfoxide.
Prepare a staining solution by adding a 1:1000 volume of 1 mM SiR-actin stock solution to the culture medium (DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Change the cell culture medium to the staining solution in the safety cabinet.
Incubate in a CO2 incubator for 0.5–1 h.
Change the medium to Leibovitz L-15 supplemented with 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Turn on the inverted fluorescence microscope (Eclipse Ti2, Nikon) equipped with the EMCCD camera (iXon Ultra 888, Andor).
Select the Cy5 filter (excitation 620/60, dichroic 660, barrier 700/75).
Adjust the excitation intensities and exposure times to avoid photobleach and phototoxicity (laser power: 1%–10%, exposure time: < 100 ms).
Take pictures.
Set up cantilevers in FIB-SEM for fabrication of FIB-milled tip.
Place a cantilever on the custom-built cantilever holder for FIB milling.
Start evacuation of the vacuum chamber.
Confirm that the pressure in the chamber is less than 5 × 10^-4 Pa.
Press “Beam On” to start the electron and ion beams.
Set the electrical voltage to 15 kV, and the current to 43 pA in SEM mode.
Adjust the focus and link the Z position of the stage and the distance between the sample and the lens.
Bring an AFM tip on the cantilever into the field of view.
Bring up the stage to 4 mm and tilt 17° with respect to the horizontal plane.
Adjust the focus and link it again.
Switch to the FIB mode and set the acceleration voltage to 16 kV and the current to 15 pA (observation mode).
Set the lowest electrical current possible for FIB mode.
Avoid unnecessary imaging to reduce unwanted milling.
Tilt the stage by 17° to achieve a 10° angle between the cantilever and ion beam line.
Increase magnification step by step up to 15,000×.
Focus on the AFM tip and record its position as “side_(cantilever number)”.
Place a rectangle area for milling inside of the probe.
Mill the tip starting from a position ∼2 μm away from the center line of the probe.
Gradually move the milling area closer to the center by decreasing electrical current.
Set the electrical current to 0.4 nA during milling operations.
Set the Properties in the Pattern Control panel to Application Si, Time 5–10 min, and Scan Direction right to left.
Scan once just before milling and confirm that the tip is not drifting.
If significant drift was observed, wait 5–10 min and readjust the milling position.
Start the milling.
When the size of the object becomes small, stop the milling and reduce the size of the milling rectangle.
Mill it again.
Replace the milling rectangle on the other side of the probe.
After milling from the side of the probe, reduce the electrical current to 15 pA.
Return the Tilt to 0° and lower the Z to 10–20 mm.
Rotate the stage by 180°.
Move the cantilever into the field of view.
Set the Z position to 4 mm and Tilt to 7°.
Focus and record the position as “front_(cantilever number)”.
Set the Scan Rotation to −90° so the probe’s tip faces up.
Place the milling rectangle on one side of the probe.
Set the electrical current to 45 pA.
Put the milling rectangle upstream of the drift first.
Scan once and start milling.
Move the rectangle to another side of the probe and mill it again.
Decrease the electrical current to 15 pA and return to the “side” position.
Place the rectangle inside the probe.
Set the electrical current to 0.13 nA.
Scan once and start milling.
Repeat the process 2–3 times while reducing the electrical current until the width of the probe is less than 200 nm.
Scan once before every milling to avoid cutting unwanted areas.
Set the electrical current to 15 pA after milling for observation.
Place a reference rectangle with a width of 180 nm at the center of the probe when the width is close to 200 nm.
Tilt the milling rectangle by 5° and taper off the tip in the front view.
Tilt the milling rectangle by −5° to continue tapering the tip.
Adjust the angle to achieve the desired tip aspect ratio.
Tilt 38° from the “side” position (total Tilt 45°).
Change to SEM mode and take a photo of the probe.
Set the cantilever in the chamber of the FIB-SEM.
Place a cantilever on the cantilever holder for EBD fabrication.
Fix the cantilever holder on the 45° inclined surface of the stage.
Close the door and start evacuation of the vacuum chamber.
Press “Beam On” to start the electron and ion beams after confirming the pressure is less than 5 × 10−4 Pa.
Set the electrical voltage to 15 kV and the current to 43 pA.
Adjust the focus on the surface and link the stage’s Z value to the distance between the sample and the lens.
Rotate the cantilever by 180°.
Bring up the stage to 4 mm.
Bring the cantilever into the field of view.
Tilt the stage by 7°.
Select the FIB mode and set the electrical voltage to 16 kV and the current to 15 pA.
Focus the AFM tip in FIB mode.
If the head of the probe is not flat, flatten the surface using FIB.
Change the electrical current to 45 pA.
Place the milling rectangle at the tip of the probe.
Take one image.
Perform milling for 2 minutes.
Deposition of carbon on the tip.
Change to SEM mode.
Set the Tilt to 35°.
Find the place for deposition.
Magnify to 150,000× and adjust focus.
Set the electrical current to 0.17 nA.
Place the deposition circle with Outer Diameter 22 nm and Dwell Time 20 minutes.
Insert the carbon GIS nozzle.
Repeat opening and closing of the nozzle a few times to release air.
Take one image.
If significant drift is observed, wait for about 5–10 minutes and readjust the position of the deposition circle.
Start deposition.
Ensure that Z is approximately 4 mm.
After deposition, retract the nozzle.
Delete the deposition circle.
Change electrical current to 45 pA.
Return to Translation 0° and Rotation 0°.
Tilt 45°.
Find tip position and take a photo.
Turn on the AFM (JPK Nanowizard 4, Bruker).
Turn on the stage controller (SPC-180713-04, Bruker).
Turn on the dish heater (RES-SAMPLE-HTR, Bruker).
Turn on the AFM-equipped fluorescence microscope (Eclipse Ti2, Nikon).
Turn on the light source (X-Cite XYLIS, Excelitas).
Turn on the EMCCD camera (iXon Ultra 888, Andor).
Set the temperature of the dish heater to 37°C.
Place the fabricated nanoneedle probe into the cantilever holder and fix it.
Place the cantilever holder on the AFM head.
Take 50 μL of the medium from the dish with a micropipette.
Fill the space between the cantilever and cantilever holder with the medium.
Place the AFM head on the stage.
Ensure space between the cantilever and the bottom of the dish.
Raise the Z-position of the AFM head if necessary.
Choose Force Spectroscopy mode.
Lower the AFM head and dip the cantilever in the medium.
Avoid touching the cell or the bottom of the dish with the tip.
Bring the cantilever into focus using a low-magnification lens (10 or 20×) while observing the bright-field image.
Align the AFM detection laser to the cantilever probe by maximizing the SUM value and centering the laser spot on the photodiode.
Calibrate the cantilever using the calibration manager of the AFM software.
Remove laser cutting and fluorescence filters if the laser spot is not found in the bright-field image.
Turn off the light of the bright field, increase the camera contrast, and find the tail of the laser spot.
Choose the data saving folder in Saving Settings and turn on Autosave.
Include Vertical Deflection data for saving.
Start the fluorescence image acquisition software (NIS-Elements, Nikon).
Change to a high-magnification lens.
Place a drop of oil on the lens if using an oil-immersion lens.
Bring the cells into focus.
Change to epifluorescence mode.
Select the Cy5 filter (excitation, 620/60; dichroic, 660; barrier, 700/75).
Take an image.
Find the cell you want to observe.
Approach the bottom surface of the dish and set the Z position as 0.
Retract the cantilever to enough height so that the nanoneedle probe does not touch the sample (10–15 μm).
Move the cantilever to the desired position on the cell.
Approach to the cell surface with a set point less than 0.5 nN for penetration.
Calculate the height of the cell to be measured.
Set the setpoint to 1–2 nN in the case of a 0.1 N/m spring constant cantilever, Z length 2 μm, Z speed 15 μm/s, 2 px/nm (sample rate 3000 Hz), approach speed 3 μm/s.
Take one force curve to measure cell surface penetration.
Adjust parameters depending on the cell type or target structure if necessary.
Change the mode to QI Advanced Imaging.
Set the setpoint to 1–2 nN, Z length 2 μm, Z speed 15 μm/s, 2 px/nm (Sample rate 3000 Hz), approach speed 3 μm/s.
Start scanning.
Set up for AC mode.
Change to AC imaging mode.
Start the AC Feedback Mode Wizard and press the Run or Infinite icon to run a frequency sweep.
Zoom into the resonance peak and set the Drive Frequency and Setpoint.
Choose the setpoint at 50%–70% of the left side of the Lock-in amplitude peak.
Set the IGain to 50–150.
Start approach.
Increase the setpoint to around 90% if imaging stops near the cell membrane.
Change the observation place or probe if needed due to imaging issues.
Wait for 2 min after adjusting settings to stabilize the nanoprobe inside the cell.
Start imaging after stabilization.
Compare trace and retrace images to confirm successful imaging.
Adjust setpoint or IGain if images do not match.
Take a force curve after 2D imaging in Force Spectroscopy mode.
Check cell height changes by comparing pre- and post-imaging force curves.
Approach the bottom of the dish and take an image of the substrate.
Compare substrate image with the 2D nanoendoscopy image to assess bottom effect.
Take the AFM head off the stage and detach the cantilever holder after measurement completion.
Remove the cantilever.
Clean the cantilever holder in ddH2O by sonication for 1 min.
Discard the dish in the waste bag for disposal of biohazard materials.
Close the AFM and fluorescence software.
Turn off all equipment that has been started up.
Clean the locking part of the cantilever holder using ddH2O and ethanol.
Clean the lens if an oil immersion lens was used with lens paper and a cleaner.
Eliminate retraction data from 3D nanoendoscopy data.
Reduce the sampling number in the Z-direction by at least half.
Flatten the image.
Subtract the background using linear fitting.
Process with a 3-pixel averaging filter.
Import the data into Voxler 4.
Visualize the upper membrane using VolRender.
Adjust the Colormap and Opacity Map as shown.
Subtract the background from the force curve using the fitted curve F(z) = A exp(-(z-z0)/λ).
Perform a 3-pixel averaging filter.
Import the data to Voxler 4 and visualize the actin filament in VolRender by setting the Colormap and Opacity Map as shown.
Calculate the differentiation of each force curve using the data after Step 9b.
Reverse the positive and negative numbers.
Import the data to Voxler 4.
Eliminate the data except where the lower membrane exists using Subset command.
Visualize the lower membrane in VolRender by setting the Colormap and Opacity Map as shown.
